extraction.name: PASTIS (Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme Series)
extraction.description: PASTIS is the first large-scale, publicly available Satellite Image Time Series (SITS) dataset with both semantic and panoptic annotations. It comprises 2,433 sequences of multi-spectral images of shape 10×128×128, with between 38 and 61 observations per sequence taken between September 2018 and November 2019. The dataset spans over 4,000 km² across four regions of France with diverse climates and crop distributions, covering almost 1% of the French Metropolitan territory. It contains over 2 billion annotated pixels and 124,422 individualized parcels, each with bounding box, pixel-precise mask, and crop type from an 18-class nomenclature plus background.
extraction.creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot, Loic Landrieu (LASTIG, Univ. Gustave Eiffel, ENSG, IGN)
extraction.publisher: LASTIG, Univ. Gustave Eiffel, ENSG, IGN
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Satellite Image Time Series were collected from the open-access Sentinel-2 platform. For each patch, all available acquisitions between September 2018 and November 2019 were stacked forming a four-dimensional multi-spectral SITS (T×C×H×W). Images were automatically filtered by the satellite data provider THEIA to remove acquisitions with extensive cloud cover.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The temporal sampling of sequences is irregular: patches are observed a different number of times (33 to 61 acquisitions) and at different intervals, due to both the orbit schedule of Sentinel-2 and the policy of Sentinel data providers not to process tile observations identified as covered by clouds for more than 90% of the tile's surface. Approximately 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover. No further pre-processing or cloud detection was applied; raw data is produced in PASTIS.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Satellite images were gathered from THEIA (value-added data processed by the CNES for the Theia data cluster using Copernicus/Sentinel-2 data). Annotations were taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS) produced by IGN, the French mapping agency.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All models are trained on batches of sequences of variable length. All-zeroes images are appended at the end of shorter sequences to match the length of the longer sequence in the batch, with a padding mask retained to prevent spatial and temporal encoding of padded values.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of Sentinel-2 (all bands except atmospheric bands B01, B09, and B10), after atmospheric correction and re-sampling at a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel. Sentinel tiles (100×100 km) are subdivided into square patches of size 1.28×1.28 km (128×128 pixels). 2,433 patches (10% of all available patches) were selected, favoring patches with rare crop types to decrease class imbalance. Parcels whose surface is more than 50% outside of the patch are annotated with the void label.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each pixel is associated with a semantic label taken from a nomenclature of 18 crop types plus a background class. Each non-background pixel also has a unique instance label corresponding to its parcel index. All annotations are taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS). Classes with at least 400 parcels and samples in at least 2 of the 4 Sentinel-2 tiles were selected, leading to an 18-class nomenclature. Parcels belonging to classes not in the 18-class nomenclature are annotated with the void label.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control over 98% and the relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Remote monitoring of the surface and nature of agricultural parcels is necessary for fair allocation of agricultural subsidies (50 and 22 billion euros per year in Europe and the US, respectively) and for ensuring that best crop rotation practices are respected. The automated analysis of SITS represents a significant interest for applications such as surveying urban development and deforestation, with important economic and environmental stakes.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes. Patches were selected favoring rare crop types to decrease class imbalance. Approximately 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The temporal sampling is irregular with variable sequence lengths (33 to 61 acquisitions). Cloud cover remains present in the dataset since no cloud detection preprocessing was applied. Class distribution is highly imbalanced. Some parcels are visually fragmented but annotated as a single instance, leading to difficult predictions. Thin parcels are difficult to detect.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of semantic and panoptic segmentation models on Satellite Image Time Series. The dataset is split into 5 folds for cross-validation, chosen with a 1 km buffer between images to avoid cross-fold contamination. Use cases include crop mapping, agricultural parcel monitoring, and benchmark evaluation of SITS encoding methods.
